sections.h2: How does property tax work in Athens-Clarke County?
sections.html:
Clarke County and the City of Athens operate as one government, so the Athens-Clarke County Property Tax Division handles the bill for the whole county. Its page explains that the money supports the Clarke County Board of Education, Athens-Clarke County and the State of Georgia.

Real estate and business personal property taxes are generally due by October 20. If a bill goes unpaid, the property can be levied on and eventually sold. The division describes a 5% penalty added every 120 days past the due date, up to four times, for a possible total of 20%, on top of interest.

  • Real property is taxed in the county where the land sits, under O.C.G.A. 48-5-11.
  • Assessed value is 40% of fair market value unless the law says otherwise, under O.C.G.A. 48-5-7.
  • Standing timber escapes tax until it is sold or cut, then it is taxed at 100% of its fair market value.

Each bill shows both the fair market value and the assessed value, so you can see what the assessors used before you decide whether to appeal.

sections.h2: What makes Clarke County different from other Georgia counties?
sections.html:
Clarke is the smallest county in Georgia by area, at 121 square miles including 1.8 of water. It lies in the Piedmont and drains mostly to the Upper Oconee River. The legislature created it on December 5, 1801 from land in Jackson County and named it for Elijah Clarke, and the county seat moved from Watkinsville to Athens in November 1871. Athens and Winterville are the municipalities, while Bogart lies mostly in Oconee County.

Its mills and railroad, which reached Athens in 1841, made it second only to Savannah and Chatham County in manufacturing investment during the 1840s. Today the University of Georgia shapes the housing market. Census QuickFacts counts 129,921 people for 2025, only 1.0% above the 2020 base, with a 2020 to 2024 median household size of 2.19 and 16.1% of residents under 18.

Only 41.4% of homes are owner occupied, the lowest rate among the four Georgia counties compared on QuickFacts, and the median gross rent is $1,219. The median owner-occupied value is $298,900, median household income is $53,625 and 73.5% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. That mix means many Athens houses are rentals, and tax bills for investor-owned homes come to the same office as owner-occupied ones.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an Athens-Clarke County assessment?
sections.html:
Appeal in writing to the Board of Assessors within 45 days of the date the assessment notice was mailed. If the Board does not change the value, the appeal goes on to the Board of Equalization automatically, and the Athens-Clarke County assessors can be reached at 706-613-3140.

Appeal timeline posted by Athens-Clarke County and the Georgia Department of Revenue
StepTiming
File written appeal with Board of AssessorsWithin 45 days of notice mailing
Board of Equalization notifies both sides of hearing dateWithin 15 days of receiving the appeal
Hearing held20 to 30 days after that notification
Appeal to Superior CourtIn writing, within 30 days of the Board of Equalization decision

At the hearing the Board of Assessors' appraiser presents comparable sales first, then you present your evidence, the Board of Equalization asks questions, and a ruling is sent to both sides. Arbitration and a hearing officer are the other two methods the state allows, and the assessors' office can explain them.

sections.h2: When must I file a return in Athens-Clarke County?
sections.html:
A real estate return on form PT-50R is filed with the tax commissioner in room 250 of the Courthouse between January 1 and April 1 of any year the property changed or was acquired. If nothing affecting value changed since last year, you may skip it. A taxpayer who fails to file a required return faces a 10% penalty on the value not returned, plus interest and possibly other penalties.

Personal property is different. Form PT-50P goes to the Board of Assessors every year by April 1, whether or not the value changed. The tax commissioner also warns buyers of businesses, boats and aircraft to check for unpaid personal property tax before closing, since attorneys usually search real estate taxes only.

sections.h2: What exemptions and refunds exist for Athens-Clarke County owners?
sections.html:
Georgia's state homestead exemption goes to people who own and occupy a home as their primary residence, and the Department of Revenue's page for Clarke County confirms that an application can be made at any time but must be in by April 1 of the first year the exemption is sought. Failing to apply counts as a waiver. Some counties add larger local exemptions, so ask the Athens-Clarke County offices which ones apply to a given house before you assume the standard amount is all there is.

Taxpayers can also ask in writing for a refund of tax that was erroneously or illegally assessed and collected, as long as the request starts within three years of payment. When an assessment is under appeal and the final taxable value comes in lower, the refund is processed automatically once that value is final. Equipment, machinery and fixtures used by a business are assessed at 40% of fair market value, and the assessor may value a going business as a whole.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes go unpaid in Athens-Clarke County?
sections.html:
Athens-Clarke County runs its own tax sales. The tax commissioner serves as ex officio sheriff, and Georgia law requires the property to be advertised for four consecutive weeks in the legal section of the county newspaper, which the county identifies as the Athens Banner-Herald.

  • Sales begin at 10:00 a.m. on the first Tuesday of the month, ordinarily in front of the courthouse, and run as a public outcry auction.
  • The opening bid equals the taxes due plus costs, and the property goes to the highest bidder or may be bid in for the county.
  • Payment is due at the sale, by cashier's or certified check from an FDIC-insured institution.
  • The tax commissioner then executes and records a tax deed. The purchaser owes taxes as they come due, and any amount paid may be added to the redemption price.

An owner who sees a notice for their address should contact the tax commissioner at once. Redemption rights exist under Georgia law, and the county's tax sale page has the current list of properties.

sections.h2: What should I settle at closing when selling in Clarke County?
sections.html:
The person who owned the property on January 1 owes tax for the full year, and Georgia gives no refund for the months after a sale. Money for the months a buyer will own the home is therefore settled between the parties on the closing statement.

Georgia also allows taxpayers 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest accrues. If the October 20 date has passed and a balance remains, ask for a payoff that includes any penalties, and have it paid from sale proceeds so the property clears.

Rental owners selling an occupied house should confirm that business personal property, such as appliances listed on a business return, has no balance. Questions about exemptions, returns or values go to the assessors, and bills and payments go to the Property Tax Division.

faqs.q: When are Athens-Clarke County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Generally by October 20. The Property Tax Division lists that as the usual due date for real estate and business personal property.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal in Athens-Clarke County?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date the assessment notice was mailed. File in writing with the Board of Assessors, and call 706-613-3140 with questions.

faqs.q: Who runs tax sales in Clarke County?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner, acting as ex officio sheriff. Sales start at 10:00 a.m. on the first Tuesday of the month, usually in front of the courthouse.

faqs.q: Do I have to file a property return every year in Athens-Clarke County?
faqs.a: Not for real estate if nothing changed. Real estate returns are due January 1 to April 1 in years the property changed or was acquired, while personal property returns are due every April 1.
No. QuickFacts shows an owner-occupied housing rate of 41.4% for 2020 to 2024, so renters hold the majority of homes.
